changes.text: 这时的国会人很少。同一天，日志记下一个付诸表决的问题：七个州出席的国会，是否有权接受总司令的辞职？日志留下了点名表决：在本篇所见的部分名单中，除帕特里奇投了反对外，其余议员均为赞成；其中埃勒里的反对票，日志记为“应该议员请求”改成了赞成。这段摘录没有显示表决结果。22日的出席记录是马萨诸塞、罗得岛、宾夕法尼亚、特拉华、马里兰、弗吉尼亚和北卡罗来纳七个州，另有新罕布什尔和南卡罗来纳各一名议员。到了23日接见当天，国会还议决立即写信给新罕布什尔、康涅狄格、纽约、新泽西、南卡罗来纳和佐治亚六个州的行政长官，催他们的代表马上到会：国会在此开会期间，出席的从未超过七个州，其中多数只有两名代表，而批准正式和约等几件要务都需要至少九个州同意。

Congress was thin at the time. The same day, the journal records a question put to the vote: "Is it the sense of Congress that seven states in Congress Assembled are competent to receive the resignation of a Commander in Chief?" The journal kept the roll call. In the portion of the roll call cited here, every member voted ay except Partridge, who voted no; Ellery's no was recorded as "changed into ay at the request of the Member". This excerpt does not show the result of the vote. On the 22nd the states present were Massachusetts, Rhode Island, Pennsylvania, Delaware, Maryland, Virginia and North Carolina, with one member each from New Hampshire and South Carolina. And on the day of the audience itself, the 23rd, Congress resolved to write at once to the executives of New Hampshire, Connecticut, New York, New Jersey, South Carolina and Georgia, demanding the immediate attendance of their delegates: during the sitting at this place there had never been more than seven states represented, most of them by only two delegates, and the ratification of the definitive treaty, among other matters, required the assent of at least nine states.

Everything in this piece rests on one source: the official Journals of the Continental Congress, volume 25 — the record of December 20 to 23, including the order of audience agreed on December 22, the audience of the twenty-third, and the text of the address. No private account by anyone present was consulted, and so the speaker's face and tone, and the reactions of individuals in the room, are beyond what this piece can know. The journal records gestures, sequence, and speech; it does not describe individual faces or reactions in the room. The address itself speaks of his being happy and pleased at the confirmation of independence, and Congress's formal answer speaks of receiving his resignation with emotions too affecting for utterance, but these are formal statements set down in writing, the answer being the institution's own written statement, not descriptions of the scene. Nor does this piece follow the man beyond that day. Motives, private thoughts, and options he may have considered are never supplied by this writer where the source is silent.

本篇所据只有《大陆会议日志》第25卷的官方记录：12月20日至23日的记录，包括12月22日议定的接见次序、23日的接见经过与讲话文本。没有取得任何在场者的私人记述，因此讲话者的神情与语气、在场个人的现场反应，本篇都无从得知。日志记动作、记次序、记讲话，不描写个人的神情与现场反应。讲话本身说到他对独立得到确认感到欣慰、高兴，国会的正式答词也自称怀着难以言表的感情接受，但这些是写成文字的正式表态，答词更是机构的书面表态，不是对现场的描写。本篇也不涉及他此后的事。凡是原文没写的动机、念头和“他考虑过的选项”，本篇都不替他补。

dispositions.rationale: 日志只写“at the request of the Member”。稿件原来译作泛指的“一位议员”，又补了一句“没有写明是哪位议员”，等于暗示提出请求的是另一位身份不明的议员，超出了证据。现在中文改为“应该议员请求”，英文只保留原引语，两种语言都删去了关于“未写明哪位议员”的断言，对请求者的身份不作推断。

evidence.quote: Ellery, no changed into ay at the request of the Member

dispositions.rationale: 检查器对 limits.0 英文的引号配对报错，把“, and Congress's formal answer says it receives ”误认作一段引文。现在把该句改为不带引号的转述：讲话说到他对独立得到确认感到 happy 与 pleased，答词说以 emotions too affecting for utterance 接受辞呈。句中不再出现引号片段，内容与证据一致，中文同步给出（实质未变）。

evidence.quote: Happy in the confirmation of our independence and sovereignty, and pleased with the opportunity
receive with emotions, too affecting for utterance
